claims.text: These three artifacts describe one and the same trip: EV-TRIP-02857, EV-GPS-02857 and EV-FARE-02857 each carry trip_id TRP-02857, and the trace window (first fix 2026-09-09T22:06:33+08:00, last fix 22:31:33) matches the trip_record's started_at and ended_at exactly. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is therefore discharged on the identifier and timing limb.

The deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01 on the governing figure. The clause makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km, and the trace records 19.12 km against a booked optimal of 14.4 km — an excess of 4.72 km, i.e. 32.78% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass: 32.78% exceeds the 20% relative threshold and 4.72 km exceeds the 0.8 km absolute threshold. No clause adjusts the optimal route here, so 4.72 km is the excess remaining for materiality.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). EV-GPS-02857 carries 151 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval with 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds and a recorded straight-line jump well under 500 m. Because no limb of POL-RD-07 fires, the corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) is not engaged, the deviation may rest on the trace alone under POL-RD-08(b), and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is closed.

The driver's explanation — the single word 'Traffic.' in his counterparty statement — carries no weight. The bundle holds no traffic_advisory for this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-02857-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with the assessor's note that no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window. I disclose that impairment expressly, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Under POL-RD-13 the traffic assertion is tested against the advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory on file that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion discharges nothing under POL-RD-08.

The absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it, and it does not escalate this case. The driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, and under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5). Two consequences follow and only two: the missing advisory is not a POL-RD-10(5) trigger, and the deviation stands at the measured 4.72 km with POL-RD-02 run against the booked optimal route, not against any amended one the driver's excuse might have suggested.

No rider-requested detour can be made out. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction from the rider in the chat_log; EV-CHAT-02857 records message_count 0 with no first or last message time, so there is no instruction to corroborate — not even one that fails the waypoint test. The clause is simply unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded from the excess on its account.

No relocation adjustment applies. Under POL-RD-05 the baseline is re-cut only where pickup or dropoff was amended after booking; EV-TRIP-02857 shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. The 14.4 km booked optimal therefore remains the baseline and no pre-amendment distance is creditable to the driver.

This is not a pooled trip. POL-RD-12 re-bases the threshold test on a matched-itinerary optimal only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL; EV-TRIP-02857 records vehicle_type RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km null. The pooled baseline the clause creates does not exist here, so the 14.4 km booked optimal is the correct comparator and the 4.72 km excess is undiluted.

The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs and the distance-and-time refund route is open. EV-FARE-02857 records fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 — which closes the distance refund on an upfront-quoted trip — does not apply to this trip and cannot be used to deny the rider the recomputation below.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation is arithmetic and points one way. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.4 + 0.28 x 19.4) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting_time_fee - 0 promo_discount = 20.832. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-02857, where it is 1.0; the trip_record carries no such field and none was inferred. Refund = charged_total 25.93 - recomputed_fare 20.832 = 5.098, which rounds UP to SGD 5.10.

Neither limiting rule disturbs that figure. The refund of 5.098 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis in POL-RD-02, so NO_ACTION cannot be taken; and 5.098 is 19.66% of charged_total, far below the 90% share at which the clause would convert the outcome to FULL_REFUND. The correct remedy is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of 5.10 against the 25.93 charged, not the 9.50 the rider asks for.

No pass-through adjustment is added or subtracted. POL-RD-09(1) provides that where a deviation is refunded under POL-RD-02, off-route ERP is already comprehended in that refund and must never be added on top of it; here EV-FARE-02857 itemises no ERP gantries at all (erp_lines total 0.00, tolls_erp 0.0), no airport surcharge, and no unmatched charge line that could support a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction. The ruling should itemise the zero ERP total for transparency and then leave the POL-RD-02 figure untouched.

PARTIAL_REFUND is a real rider win on these facts. The rider filed this dispute, and under POL-GEN-03 the ruling values are defined against the filing party: EV-FARE-02857 shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the present state is that the rider carries the whole 25.93. A partial refund of 5.10 is money returned to the rider and reduces the charge they carry; NO_ACTION, by contrast, would leave that charge exactly where it is.

I concede the rider's stated ground and do not press it. The 'six deviation flags' in the claim text is driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags, a LIFETIME counter; POL-RD-06 asks for driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting one for the other. On the citable trailing figure the driver's record is clean: deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 260, so no repeat pattern is established, and the excess here (32.78%, 4.72 km) is below both materiality gates of 50% and 8.0 km, so POL-RD-06 is not even engaged on materiality. The rider's request for FULL_REFUND is not supported by the record and I do not ask the Judge to grant it; the 5.10 arithmetic above is what the policy provides.

The raised corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 does not fire against this rider. That condition requires rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d of 4 or more with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 1 or fewer; EV-RPROF-02857 shows deviation_claims_60d of 1 and a substantiated count of 0, and this trip's excess of 32.78% is in any event above the 30% floor at which the extra requirement would attach. No corroboration beyond the unimpaired trace is needed to prove the excess.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, so the rider is entitled to a moneyed ruling rather than a held file. The identifiers on trip_record, trace and fare_breakdown all match; the trace is unimpaired so POL-RD-10(3) is not reached; no timestamps conflict or run backwards; no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a cited artifact, because the driver cited none; the refund of 5.10 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total; and no charge line lacks a counterpart. The one absent artifact, the traffic advisory, is a bundle gap that POL-RD-13(1) directs be treated as weightless rather than as a contradiction.

claims.text: The rider's demand for a full refund is built on the wrong field. Her claim points to six deviation flags; that is driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags, a LIFETIME counter, and POL-GEN-01 marks that field as CONTEXT ONLY and forbids it as a ground of decision. The field POL-RD-06 actually names is driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, which stands at 0 against 260 completed trips in the same 90-day window - below both limbs of the pattern test, which needs 3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more on at least 40 completed trips. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are both unavailable, and the rider's characterisation of the driver's record is contradicted by the only citable counter on the profile.

On this trip's own trace the excess is 4.72 km and 32.78 percent of the 14.4 km booked optimal. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20 percent, but sits below both materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50 percent, so the deviation is established and NOT material - and materiality is the only condition that engages the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check on this trip. The remedy is therefore confined to the POL-RD-02 arithmetic; a 4.72 km overshoot on a 25-minute metered trip is not the serial-misconduct case the rider's claim asserts.

The most the rider can recover is SGD 5.10, and the fare ledger proves it: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.4 + 0.28 x 19.4) x 1.0 (the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 20.8320; refund = charged_total 25.93 - 20.8320 = 5.0980, rounded UP to SGD 5.10. That is 19.66 percent of charged_total - above the 0.50 de minimis, so a refund is due rather than NO_ACTION, but far below the 90 percent share that would convert it into a full refund. The rider's 9.50 figure has no line of the fare_breakdown behind it.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. The ledger carries no ERP or toll lines at all - on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP both 0.00 - and no airport surcharge on a trip that does not originate at an airport, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction and no POL-RD-09 pass-through refund arises. The billed distance of 19.1 km matches the trace's 19.12 km to within 20 metres, so the rider was not billed for distance the vehicle did not drive. The rider's recovery is the difference against the optimal route and nothing more.

Nothing else in the bundle supports a remedy beyond that arithmetic. There is no chat log for the trip - 0 messages, so no rider instruction of any kind was recorded - and the bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02857-01, is IMPAIRED BY ABSENCE: it carries no payload, its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT with severity BLOCKING, so it can establish no fact for either party and the POL-RD-03 advisory comparison cannot be run on this record. The driver's contemporaneous account of traffic therefore stands unrefuted by any artifact in the bundle, but the driver does not ask the tribunal to assume a closure the record never records: the rider's case is the trace excess, and the trace excess is fully answered by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic figure.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. This was a metered RYDE_X trip, TRP-02857, driven on 2026-09-09. The booked optimal route was 14.4 km (EV-TRIP-02857). The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02857, weight 1.0), which records 19.12 km against the booked optimal, an excess of 4.72 km, or 32.78%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (above 0.8 km and above 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED; neither materiality gate (8.0 km, 50%) is met, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation. The trace itself is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 151 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and no jump over 500 m, so the deviation rests on the trace alone (POL-RD-08(b)) and no POL-RD-07(ii)/POL-RD-10(3) corroboration question arises. The triad EV-TRIP-02857 / EV-GPS-02857 / EV-FARE-02857 all carry trip_id TRP-02857 with matching timing, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied. No exculpatory clause applies: EV-CHAT-02857 has 0 messages (POL-RD-04 has no instruction to test), no pickup or dropoff amendment exists (POL-RD-05), and the vehicle is RYDE_X with no pooled itinerary (POL-RD-12). POL-RD-11 does not apply because the fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-02 runs. The arithmetic, read off EV-FARE-02857: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.4 + 0.28 x 19.4) x 1.0 surge multiplier (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 20.832; charged_total 25.93; refund = 25.93 - 20.832 = 5.098, rounded UP to SGD 5.10. ledger.claim: The rider's demand for a full refund is built on the wrong field. Her claim points to six deviation flags; that is driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags, a LIFETIME counter, and POL-GEN-01 marks that field as CONTEXT ONLY and forbids it as a ground of decision. The field POL-RD-06 actually names is driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d, which stands at 0 against 260 completed trips in the same 90-day window - below both limbs of the pattern test, which needs 3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more on at least 40 completed trips. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are both unavailable, and the rider's characterisation of the driver's record is contradicted by the only citable counter on the profile.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_deviation_flags

ledger.claim: On this trip's own trace the excess is 4.72 km and 32.78 percent of the 14.4 km booked optimal. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20 percent, but sits below both materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50 percent, so the deviation is established and NOT material - and materiality is the only condition that engages the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check on this trip. The remedy is therefore confined to the POL-RD-02 arithmetic; a 4.72 km overshoot on a 25-minute metered trip is not the serial-misconduct case the rider's claim asserts.

The most the rider can recover is SGD 5.10, and the fare ledger proves it: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 14.4 + 0.28 x 19.4) x 1.0 (the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 20.8320; refund = charged_total 25.93 - 20.8320 = 5.0980, rounded UP to SGD 5.10. That is 19.66 percent of charged_total - above the 0.50 de minimis, so a refund is due rather than NO_ACTION, but far below the 90 percent share that would convert it into a full refund. The rider's 9.50 figure has no line of the fare_breakdown behind it.

Nothing may be added on top of that figure. The ledger carries no ERP or toll lines at all - on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP both 0.00 - and no airport surcharge on a trip that does not originate at an airport, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction and no POL-RD-09 pass-through refund arises. The billed distance of 19.1 km matches the trace's 19.12 km to within 20 metres, so the rider was not billed for distance the vehicle did not drive. The rider's recovery is the difference against the optimal route and nothing more.

Nothing else in the bundle supports a remedy beyond that arithmetic. There is no chat log for the trip - 0 messages, so no rider instruction of any kind was recorded - and the bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02857-01, is IMPAIRED BY ABSENCE: it carries no payload, its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT with severity BLOCKING, so it can establish no fact for either party and the POL-RD-03 advisory comparison cannot be run on this record. The driver's contemporaneous account of traffic therefore stands unrefuted by any artifact in the bundle, but the driver does not ask the tribunal to assume a closure the record never records: the rider's case is the trace excess, and the trace excess is fully answered by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic figure.
